name: Form
description: A Form object refers to a particular Microsoft Access form.
remarks: A Form object is a member of the Forms collection, which is a collection of all currently open forms. Within the Forms collection, individual forms are indexed beginning with zero. Refer to an individual Form object in the Forms collection either by referring to the form by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. If you want to refer to a specific form in the Forms collection, it's better to refer to the form by name because a form's collection index may change. If the form name includes a space, the name must be surrounded by brackets ([ ]). Each Form object has a Controls collection, which contains all controls on the form. Refer to a control on a form either by implicitly or explicitly referring to the Controls collection. Your code will be faster if you refer to the Controls collection implicitly. The following examples show two of the ways you might refer to a control named NewData on the form called OrderForm. The next two examples show how you might refer to a control named NewData on a subform ctlSubForm contained in the form called OrderForm.
example:
Private Sub cmdSearch_Click()

   Dim db As DAO.Database
   Dim qd As QueryDef
   Dim vWhere As Variant

   Set db = CurrentDb()

   On Error Resume Next
   db.QueryDefs.Delete "Query1"
   On Error GoTo 0

   vWhere = Null

   vWhere = vWhere & " AND [PayeeID]=" + Me.cboPayeeID

   If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") <> "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") <> "" Then
      vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed] Between #" & _
      Me.txtStartDate & "# AND #" & Me.txtEndDate & "#"
   Else
      If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") = "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") <> "" Then
         vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed]>=#" _
                  + Me.txtStartDate & "#"
      Else
         If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") <> "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") = "" Then
            vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed] <=#" _
                     + Me.txtEndDate & "#"
      End If
     End If
   End If

   If Nz(vWhere, "") = "" Then
      MsgBox "There are no search criteria selected." & vbCrLf & vbCrLf & _
             "Search Cancelled.", vbInformation, "Search Canceled."
   Else
      Set qd = db.CreateQueryDef("Query1", "SELECT * FROM tblRefundData? & _
               " WHERE " & Mid(vWhere, 6))
      db.Close
      Set db = Nothing

      DoCmd.OpenQuery "Query1", acViewNormal, acReadOnly
   End If
End Sub

properties.name: UseDefaultPrinter
properties.description: Returns or sets a Boolean indicating whether the specified form uses the default printer for the system; True if the form or report uses the default printer. Read/write.

properties.name: RecordSourceQualifier
properties.description: Returns or sets a String indicating the SQL Server owner name of the record source for the specified form. Read/write.

properties.name: FilterOnLoad
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the filter specified by the Filter property is applied when the form is loaded. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: OrderByOnLoad
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the sorting specified by the OrderBy property is applied when the form is loaded. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: SplitFormOrientation
properties.description: Gets or sets the position of the datasheet relative to the form when the form is displayed in Split Form view. Read/write AcSplitFormOrientation.

properties.name: SplitFormDatasheet
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the user can edit records in the datasheet when a form is displayed in Split Form view. Read/write AcSplitFormDatasheet.

properties.name: SplitFormSplitterBar
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the splitter bar is available when the form is displayed in Split Form mode. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: SplitFormPrinting
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the contents of the form or the datasheet are printed when printing a form displayed in Split Form view. Read/write AcSplitFormPrinting.

properties.name: SplitFormSplitterBarSave
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the location of the splitter bar is saved when a form that's displayed in Split Form mode is closed. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: NavigationCaption
properties.description: Gets or sets the text that appears to the left of the form's navigation buttons. Read/write String.

properties.name: AllowLayoutView
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the specified form can be used in Layout view. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: DatasheetAlternateBackColor
properties.description: Gets or sets the color displayed on alternate rows of a form's datasheet. Read/write Long.

properties.name: DisplayOnSharePointSite
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the specified form can be made available as a view on a Microsoft SharePoint Foundation site. Read/write Byte.

properties.name: SplitFormSize
properties.description: Gets or sets the size in twips of the form when it's displayed in Split Form view. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Section
properties.description: Use the Section property to identify a section of a form and provide access to the properties of that section. Read-only Section object.

properties.name: RibbonName
properties.description: Gets or sets the name of the customized ribbon to be displayed when the specified form is loaded. Read/write String.

properties.name: FitToScreen
properties.description: Gets or sets whether the width of the form is reduced to fit the width of the screen. Read/write Boolean.

methods.name: Undo
methods.description: Use the Undo method to reset a control or form when its value has been changed.

methods.name: Recalc
methods.description: The Recalc method immediately updates all calculated controls on a form.

methods.name: Requery
methods.description: The Requery method updates the data underlying a specified form by requerying the source of data for the form.

methods.name: Refresh
methods.description: The Refresh method immediately updates the records in the underlying record source for a specified form or datasheet to reflect changes made to the data by you and other users in a multiuser environment.

methods.name: Repaint
methods.description: The Repaint method completes any pending screen updates for a specified form. When performed on a form, the Repaint method also completes any pending recalculations of the form's controls.

methods.name: GoToPage
methods.signature: GoToPage(PageNumber As Long, [Right As Long], [Down As Long])
methods.description: The GoToPage method moves the focus to the first control on a specified page in the active form.

parameters.name: PageNumber
parameters.description: A numeric expression that's a valid page number for the active form.

parameters.name: Right
parameters.description: A numeric expression that's a valid horizontal offset (in twips) from the left side of the window to the part of the page to be viewed.

parameters.name: Down
parameters.description: A numeric expression that's a valid vertical offset (in twips) from the top of the window to the part of the page to be viewed.

methods.name: SetFocus
methods.description: The SetFocus method moves the focus to the specified form, the specified control on the active form, or the specified field on the active datasheet.

methods.name: Move
methods.signature: Move(Left As Variant, [Top As Variant], [Width As Variant], [Height As Variant])
methods.description: Moves the specified object to the coordinates specified by the argument values.

parameters.name: Left
parameters.description: The screen position in twips for the left edge of the object relative to the left edge of the Microsoft Access window.

parameters.name: Top
parameters.description: The screen position in twips for the top edge of the object relative to the top edge of the Access window.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The desired width of the object in twips.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The desired height of the object in twips.

events.name: Load
events.description: Occurs when a form is opened and its records are displayed.

events.name: Current
events.description: Occurs when the focus moves to a record, making it the current record, or when the form is refreshed or requeried.

events.name: BeforeInsert
events.description: The BeforeInsert event occurs when the user types the first character in a new record, but before the record is actually created.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the BeforeInsert event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the BeforeInsert event.

events.name: AfterInsert
events.description: The AfterInsert event occurs after a new record is added.

events.name: Delete
events.description: Occurs when the user performs some action, such as pressing the Delete key, to delete a record, but before the record is actually deleted.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the Delete event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the Delete event.

events.name: BeforeDelConfirm
events.signature: BeforeDelConfirm(Cancel As Integer, Response As Integer)
events.description: The BeforeDelConfirm event occurs after the user deletes to the buffer one or more records, but before Microsoft Access displays a dialog box asking the user to confirm the deletions.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the BeforeDelConfirm event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True cancels the BeforeDelConfirm event and prevents the Delete Confirm dialog box from being displayed. If the event is canceled, the original records are restored, but the AfterDelConfirm event still occurs. If Cancel is set to True, the Response argument is ignored. If Cancel is set to False (0), which it is by default, the value in the Response argument is used by Access to determine the type of response to the Delete event.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description: An intrinsic constant that determines whether Access displays the Delete Confirm dialog box asking if the record should be deleted. acDataErrContinue continues without displaying the Delete Confirm dialog box. Setting the Cancel argument to False and the Response argument to acDataErrContinue enables Microsoft Access to delete records without prompting the user. acDataErrDisplay displays the Delete Confirm dialog box. The default value is acDataErrDisplay.

events.name: AfterDelConfirm
events.description: The AfterDelConfirm event occurs after the user confirms that the deletions and the records are actually deleted or when the deletions are canceled.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: An intrinsic constant that indicates whether a record has been deleted. acDeleteOK indicates that the deletion was successful. acDeleteCancel indicates that the deletion was canceled in Visual Basic. acDeleteUserCancel indicates that the deletion was canceled by the user.

events.name: Open
events.description: The Open event occurs when a form is opened, but before the first record is displayed.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the opening of the form or report occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the opening of the form or report.

events.name: Resize
events.description: The Resize event occurs when a form is opened and whenever the size of a form changes.

events.name: Unload
events.description: The Unload event occurs after a form is closed but before it's removed from the screen. When the form is reloaded, Microsoft Access redisplays the form and reinitializes the contents of all its controls.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Set to True to cancel the Unload event.

events.name: Close
events.description: The Close event occurs when a form is closed and removed from the screen.

events.name: Activate
events.description: The Activate event occurs when a form receives the focus and becomes the active window.

events.name: Deactivate
events.description: The Deactivate event occurs when a form loses the focus to a Table, Query, Form, Report, Macro, or Module window, or to the Database window.

events.name: GotFocus
events.description: The GotFocus event occurs when the specified object receives the focus.

events.name: LostFocus
events.description: The LostFocus event occurs when the specified object loses the focus.

events.name: Click
events.description: The Click event occurs when the user presses and then releases a mouse button over an object.

events.name: DblClick
events.description: The DblClick event occurs when the user presses and releases the left mouse button twice over an object within the double-click time limit of the system.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the DblClick event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the DblClick event.

events.name: MouseDown
events.signature: MouseDown(Button As Integer, Shift As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single)
events.description: The MouseDown event occurs when the user presses a mouse button.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
The button that was pressed to trigger the event. If you need to test for the Button argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acLeftButton The bit mask for the left mouse button.

  • acRightButton The bit mask for the right mouse button.

  • acMiddleButton The bit mask for the middle mouse button.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the Button argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The x coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The y coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

events.name: MouseMove
events.signature: MouseMove(Button As Integer, Shift As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single)
events.description: The MouseMove event occurs when the user moves the mouse.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
The button that was pressed or released when the event was triggered. If you need to test for the Button argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acLeftButton The bit mask for the left mouse button.

  • acRightButton The bit mask for the right mouse button.

  • acMiddleButton The bit mask for the middle mouse button.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the Button argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The x coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The y coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

events.name: MouseUp
events.signature: MouseUp(Button As Integer, Shift As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single)
events.description: The MouseUp event occurs when the user releases a mouse button.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
The button that was released to trigger the event. If you need to test for the Button argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acLeftButton The bit mask for the left mouse button.

  • acRightButton The bit mask for the right mouse button.

  • acMiddleButton The bit mask for the middle mouse button.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the Button argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The x coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The y coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

events.name: KeyDown
events.signature: KeyDown(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyDown event occurs when the user presses a key while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting KeyCode to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: KeyPress
events.description: The KeyPress event occurs when the user presses and releases a key or key combination that corresponds to an ANSI code while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send an ANSI keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyAscii
parameters.description: Returns a numeric ANSI key code. The KeyAscii argument is passed by reference; changing it sends a different character to the object. Setting the KeyAscii argument to 0 cancels the keystroke so that the object doesn't recognize that a key was pressed.

events.name: KeyUp
events.signature: KeyUp(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyUp event occurs when the user releases a key while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting KeyCode to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: Error
events.signature: Error(DataErr As Integer, Response As Integer)
events.description: The Error event occurs when a run-time error is produced in Microsoft Access when a form has the focus.

parameters.name: DataErr
parameters.description: The error code returned by the Err object when an error occurs. Use the DataErr argument with the Error function to map the number to the corresponding error message.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description:
The setting determines whether an error message is displayed. The Response argument can be one of the following intrinsic constants.

  • acDataErrContinue Ignore the error and continue without displaying the default Microsoft Access error message. You can supply a custom error message in place of the default error message.

  • acDataErrDisplay (Default) Display the default Access error message.

events.name: Timer
events.description: The Timer event occurs for a form at regular intervals as specified by the form's TimerInterval property.

events.name: Filter
events.signature: Filter(Cancel As Integer, FilterType As Integer)
events.description: Occurs when the user opens a filter window by choosing Filter by Form, Advanced Filter/Sort, or Server Filter By Form.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines whether to open the filter window. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) prevents the filter window from opening. You can also use the CancelEvent method of the DoCmd object to cancel opening the filter window.

parameters.name: FilterType
parameters.description:
The filter window the user is trying to open. The FilterType argument can be one of the following intrinsic constants:
  • acFilterByForm
  • acFilterAdvanced
  • acServerFilterByForm

events.name: ApplyFilter
events.signature: ApplyFilter(Cancel As Integer, ApplyType As Integer)
events.description: Occurs when a filter is applied to a form.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the ApplyFilter event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True cancels the ApplyFilter event and the filter is not applied to the form.

parameters.name: ApplyType
parameters.description: Returns the type of filter that was applied.

events.name: Dirty
events.description: The Dirty event occurs when the contents of the specified control changes.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the Dirty event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the Dirty event.

events.name: Undo
events.description: Occurs when the user undoes a change.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Set this argument to True to cancel the undo operation and leave the control or form in its edited state.

events.name: OnConnect
events.description: Occurs when the specified PivotTable view connects to a data source.

events.name: OnDisconnect
events.description: Occurs when the specified PivotTable view disconnects from a data source.

events.name: PivotTableChange
events.description: Occurs whenever the specified PivotTable view field, field set, or total is added or deleted.

parameters.name: Reason
parameters.description: A PivotTableReasonEnum constant that indicates how the PivotTable list changed.

events.name: Query
events.description: Occurs whenever the specified PivotTable view query becomes necessary. The query may not occur immediately; it may be delayed until the new data is displayed.

events.name: BeforeQuery
events.description: Occurs when the specified PivotTable view queries its data source.

events.name: SelectionChange
events.description: Occurs whenever the user makes a new selection in a PivotChart view or PivotTable view.

events.name: CommandBeforeExecute
events.signature: CommandBeforeExecute(Command As Variant, Cancel As Object)
events.description: Occurs before a specified command is executed. Use this event when you want to impose certain restrictions before a particular command is executed.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: The command that is going to be executed.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Set the Value property of this object to True to cancel the command.

events.name: CommandChecked
events.signature: CommandChecked(Command As Variant, Checked As Object)
events.description: Occurs when the specified Microsoft Office web component determines whether the specified command is selected.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: The command that has been verified as being selected.

parameters.name: Checked
parameters.description: Set the Value property of this object to False to clear the command.

events.name: CommandEnabled
events.signature: CommandEnabled(Command As Variant, Enabled As Object)
events.description: Occurs when the specified Microsoft Office web component determines whether the specified command is enabled.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: The command that has been verified as being enabled.

parameters.name: Enabled
parameters.description: Set the Value property of this object to False to disable the command.

events.name: CommandExecute
events.description: Occurs after the specified command is executed. Use this event when you want to execute a set of commands after a particular command is executed.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: The command that is executed.

events.name: DataSetChange
events.description: Occurs whenever the specified PivotTable view is data-bound and the data set changes; for example, when a filter operation takes place. This event also occurs when initial data is available from the data source.

events.name: BeforeScreenTip
events.signature: BeforeScreenTip(ScreenTipText As Object, SourceObject As Object)
events.description: Occurs before a ScreenTip is displayed for an element in a PivotChart view or PivotTable view.

parameters.name: ScreenTipText
parameters.description: Set the Value property of this object to the ScreenTip that you want to display. Changing this argument to an empty string effectively hides the ScreenTip.

parameters.name: SourceObject
parameters.description: The object that generates the ScreenTip.

events.name: BeforeRender
events.signature: BeforeRender(drawObject As Object, chartObject As Object, Cancel As Object)
events.description: Occurs before any object in the specified PivotChart view has been rendered.

parameters.name: drawObject
parameters.description: A reference to the ChChartDraw object. Use the DrawType property of the returned object to determine what type of rendering is about to occur.

parameters.name: chartObject
parameters.description: The object that is to be rendered. Use the TypeName function to determine the type of the object.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Set the Value property of this object to True to cancel the rendering of the PivotChart view object.

events.name: AfterRender
events.signature: AfterRender(drawObject As Object, chartObject As Object)
events.description: Occurs after the object represented by the chartObject argument has been rendered.

parameters.name: drawObject
parameters.description: A ChChartDraw object. Use the methods and properties of this object to draw objects on the chart.

parameters.name: chartObject
parameters.description: The object that has just been rendered. Use the TypeName function to determine what type of object has just been rendered.

events.name: AfterFinalRender
events.description: Occurs after all elements in the specified PivotChart view have been rendered.

parameters.name: drawObject
parameters.description: A ChChartDraw object. Use the methods and properties of this object to draw objects on the chart.

events.name: AfterLayout
events.description: Occurs after all charts in the specified PivotChart view have been laid out, but before they have been rendered.

parameters.name: drawObject
parameters.description: A ChChartDraw object. Use the methods and properties of this object to draw objects on the chart.

events.name: MouseWheel
events.signature: MouseWheel(Page As Boolean, Count As Long)
events.description: Occurs when the user rolls the mouse wheel in Form view, Split Form view, Datasheet view, Layout view, PivotChart view, or PivotTable view.

parameters.name: Page
parameters.description: True if the page was changed.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: The number of lines by which the view was scrolled with the mouse wheel.

events.name: ViewChange
events.description: Occurs whenever the specified PivotChart view or PivotTable view is redrawn.

parameters.name: Reason
parameters.description: A PivotViewReasonEnum constant that indicates how the view was changed. Reason always returns 1 for PivotChart views.

events.name: DataChange
events.description: Occurs when certain properties are changed or when certain methods are executed in the specified PivotTable view.

parameters.name: Reason
parameters.description: A PivotDataReasonEnum constant that indicates the reason that this event was triggered.
